b2-amazoniapan-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Why a Treaty
b2-amazoniapan-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading about the Amazon Cooperation Treaty, and he asks why the countries created a permanent secretariat.
b2-amazoniapan-01.prompt: Tell Carlos that the countries created a secretariat so that cooperation would be permanent.
b2-amazoniapan-01.target: Los países crearon una secretaría para que la cooperación fuera permanente.
b2-amazoniapan-01.english: The countries created a secretariat so that cooperation would be permanent.
b2-amazoniapan-01.canDo: I can say what an agreement or a meeting is for with *para que* + subjunctive, about the Amazon Treaty.

b2-amazoniapan-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Open Border
b2-amazoniapan-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading about Leticia and Tabatinga, and she asks whether a fence divides the cities.
b2-amazoniapan-02.prompt: Tell Meg that there is no fence that separates the two cities.
b2-amazoniapan-02.target: No hay ninguna valla que separe las dos ciudades.
b2-amazoniapan-02.english: There is no fence that separates the two cities.
b2-amazoniapan-02.canDo: I can tell a real thing from one that is only wanted or does not exist with *que* + indicative or subjunctive, about the Amazon borders.

b2-amazoniapan-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Andes and the Rain
b2-amazoniapan-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a talk about the Amazon's water cycle, and he asks why the humid air goes south.
b2-amazoniapan-03.prompt: Tell Carlos that, because of the Andes, the humid air turns south.
b2-amazoniapan-03.target: Debido a los Andes, el aire húmedo se desvía hacia el sur.
b2-amazoniapan-03.english: Because of the Andes, the humid air turns south.
b2-amazoniapan-03.canDo: I can give a cause in a formal way with *debido a* and *a raíz de*, about the Amazon's water cycle.

b2-amazoniapan-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Mercury in the River
b2-amazoniapan-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading a report about mercury, and she asks what the presence of mercury in fish suggests.
b2-amazoniapan-04.prompt: Tell Meg that if the fish have mercury there must be mines nearby, as a guess.
b2-amazoniapan-04.target: Si los peces tienen mercurio, debe de haber minas cerca.
b2-amazoniapan-04.english: If the fish have mercury, there must be mines nearby.
b2-amazoniapan-04.canDo: I can say how sure I am with *puede*, *debe de* and *tiene que* + infinitive, about mercury in the Amazon rivers.

b2-amazoniapan-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Different Past
b2-amazoniapan-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading about the standing forest, and he asks what difference less logging would have made.
b2-amazoniapan-05.prompt: Tell Carlos that if fewer trees had been cut down in the last century there would be more forest today.
cues: Say what there would be today
b2-amazoniapan-05.target: Si no se hubieran talado tantos árboles en el siglo XX, hoy habría más bosque.
b2-amazoniapan-05.english: If so many trees had not been cut down in the 20th century, there would be more forest today.
b2-amazoniapan-05.canDo: I can say how a different past would change the present with *si hubiera* + participle and the conditional, about the Amazon.

b2-amazoniapan-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Amazon in Review
b2-amazoniapan-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing a short talk about the Amazon basin, and she asks you to describe the border between the two cities.
b2-amazoniapan-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what eight countries signed in 1978 and why.
cues: Say what they signed and when
b2-amazoniapan-consolidation.target: Ocho países firmaron en 1978 el Tratado de Cooperación Amazónica para trabajar juntos.
b2-amazoniapan-consolidation.english: Eight countries signed the Amazon Cooperation Treaty in 1978 to work together.
b2-amazoniapan-consolidation.canDo: I can review what I learned about the Amazon basin, from the treaty to the standing forest.
